Tired of babysitting your AI coding assistants? 🤖

Claw Code is a fully autonomous, agent-managed Rust CLI harness built to execute, verify, and preserve software development tasks with zero human intervention. 

Building fully autonomous developer agents usually means wrestling with fragile scripting or performance bottlenecks. Claw Code solves this by providing a robust, memory-safe Rust CLI framework that plans, executes, verifies, and manages software engineering workflows independently.

Top Features:
🦀 Native Rust workspace delivering a high-performance CLI binary for agent orchestration
🩺 Built-in doctor diagnostic tooling to verify system wiring, auth, and environments
💻 Comprehensive platform support for macOS, Linux, and PowerShell-first Windows
🔌 Flexible provider setup supporting Anthropic API keys, local OpenAI-compatible models, and offline skill installations

Whether you want to study advanced agent harness design in Rust, deploy local offline coding agents, or prototype zero-human-intervention workflows, this is your blueprint.

🚀 Unlock 2x Tensor Throughput on Your RTX 4090! 

Are artificial performance limits slowing down your local AI training and LLM fine-tuning? 

Meet gpu-unlock-ada, the open-source Linux kernel module and firmware pipeline that bypasses artificial speed restrictions on high-end consumer NVIDIA Ada Lovelace GPUs. By applying an SM speed-select override before the stock proprietary driver initializes, this tool restores full tensor instruction throughput—doubling FP16 and BF16 rates with FP32 accumulation on cards like the RTX 4090, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, and RTX 4060 Ti 16GB. 

Achieve near data-center class compute efficiency on your local workstation without paying enterprise-tier prices!

✨ Key Features:
• Pre-Driver Initialization: Configures SM speed-select registers and executes a PCIe Function Level Reset before the NVIDIA driver binds.
• Automated Pipeline: Generates and packages local firmware seamlessly with support for Arch Linux, Debian, and RPM build systems.
• Initramfs Integration: Works natively with mkinitcpio, initramfs-tools, and dracut to guarantee the unlock sequence fires on early boot.
• Target Hardware Support: Explicit PCI address binding for popular high-end consumer workstation GPUs.

Perfect for AI researchers, ML engineers, and HPC developers looking to maximize local PyTorch and TensorFlow matrix multiplication performance. 

Check out the repository and supercharge your local GPU cluster today:
https://github.com/JustAResearcher/gpu-unlock-ada

Tired of your productivity apps eating all your RAM just to display text? Say goodbye to Electron bloat. 🚀

Meet ElyOffice: a native, GPU-accelerated offline-first desktop suite built entirely in Rust and GPUI. 

The Problem:
Modern desktop productivity apps are heavy, sluggish, resource-intensive, and constantly tethered to the cloud. They demand accounts, subscriptions, and stream your data to remote servers. 

The Solution:
ElyOffice brings native performance back to your desktop. It is a comprehensive office suite featuring document editors, PDF tools, a mail client, and a Git client that operates entirely locally on your files with zero telemetry and zero cloud lock-in.

Key Features:
⚡ GPU-Accelerated UI: Powered by GPUI and Rust for instantaneous responsiveness and minimal memory consumption.
📄 Robust Core Engines: Leverages LibreOfficeKit for documents and spreadsheets, MuPDF and Tesseract for advanced PDF handling, and custom Rust engines for mail and markdown.
🔒 True Offline-First: All files stay strictly on your local drive. No accounts, no subscriptions, no forced cloud dependencies.
cross-platform: Fully optimized for Windows, macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon), and Linux.

Why Developers Will Love It:
For Rustaceans and desktop engineers, ElyOffice serves as an incredible architectural blueprint and reference implementation. It demonstrates how to integrate heavy C and C++ upstream engines into a memory-safe Rust workspace, manage complex multi-platform build scripts, and build production-grade, GPU-rendered desktop apps from scratch.

Check out the source code, star the project, and start building better native apps today:
https://github.com/ELY-Open-Source/ElyOffice

Ever wondered if you could boot Apple's XNU kernel and stock iOS 16.5 user space natively on Qualcomm Android hardware? 

Running proprietary Apple operating systems on foreign hardware used to be a pipe dream. Security researchers and low-level engineers often hit a wall when trying to inspect kernel internals without bricking physical devices or dealing with rigid hardware locks.

HakiOS solves this by providing an experimental research bench that boots Apple's XNU kernel and stock iOS user space (launchd, SpringBoard, and apps) on non-Apple hardware like Qualcomm-powered Android devices and QEMU virtual machines. Best of all? It injects a custom UEFI bootloader into RAM via fastboot, eliminating the need to flash your phone.

Here is what makes it a game-changer for systems engineers:

* Cross-Architecture Kernel Porting: Adapts the XNU kernel to run on ARM64 Qualcomm SoCs using custom C device drivers.
* Dynamic Hardware Abstraction: Leverages native Android device trees, firmware, and power rails at runtime.
* Modem & DSP Integration: Interfaces with Qualcomm's Hexagon MPSS modem, audio DSP, and IPA packet engine straight from XNU.
* QEMU Virtualization Support: Test the full stack locally without risking physical hardware.

Get deep visibility into kernel-level architecture, hybrid OS design, and low-level boot flows today. 

Check out the repo and start experimenting:
https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-kernel
